checks.claim: An air conditioner's compressor squeezes refrigerant gas, which makes it hot, and the condenser coil releases that heat outside.
checks.why: Compressing the refrigerant raises its temperature above the outdoor air; at the condenser coil the heat flows out and the refrigerant turns liquid (Carrier, Trane, Penn State).

sources.title: HVAC Basics: How Does an Air Conditioner Work? (Trane)

checks.claim: Portable air conditioners vent their hot air outside through a hose fitted into a window panel kit.
checks.why: Portable units ship with an exhaust hose and adjustable window seal panels; foam strips seal the gaps round the sash.

sources.title: Portable AC window kit installation sheet (Sylvane)
Portable air con window seal kit

checks.claim: An air conditioner's cold coil pulls water out of the air, which drips into a drain pan and runs out a drain line.
checks.why: Moisture in humid indoor air condenses on the cold evaporator coil, falls into a pan below, and a condensate drain line carries it away.

sources.title: What Is a Condensate Drain Line? (Angi)
